source.title: MI-MIDI 2: From Observation to Control with Sparse Autoencoders in Text-to-MIDI Generation

record.tranche_reason: The study investigates SAE feature characterization and steering in text-to-MIDI models, but it does not test feature splitting as dictionary size grows. It reports a limited cross-dictionary feature-matching result, which is related to feature consistency but does not measure splitting, input partitioning, or decomposition into smaller-dictionary features.
record.gate_note: The paper trains dictionaries at specified sizes and measures whether one synth-lead feature has a close counterpart in other dictionaries. This is not a dictionary-size sweep for splitting: it does not test whether a coarse feature is replaced by finer features, whether their inputs partition the coarse feature's inputs, or whether their directions are nearby. The steering and observational results concern other questions and are not rows for these claim versions.
record.test_reason: The paper trains TopK SAEs on text2midi and MIDI-LLM to test whether observational evidence predicts steering. It never measures or discusses feature splitting, absorption or hierarchy; it cites Bricken et al. only as an SAE method. The cross-dictionary matching (EF8 vs EF8 and EF8 vs EF4 at text2midi L13) checks whether features recur across independently trained runs. It does not check whether a coarse feature splits into finer ones, whether inputs are partitioned, or whether features decompose into combinations. The EF4 vs EF8 match-rate difference (25.6% vs 35.2%) is also confounded with seed and run differences, so it cannot speak to V5. I changed the reader's 'discusses' to 'cites_only' because splitting is not discussed in the text.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that a description-identified synth-lead feature steered its instrument program in a prespecified confirmation and a replication, and reappeared in independently trained dictionaries. Density-adjusted correlation features showed a small family-level shift, while raw-correlation features showed none. They caution that single-run dictionaries support the stability of that one feature, not of whole dictionaries.
record.recipe_differences: The study does not test the original feature-splitting method or a dictionary-size sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: The cross-dictionary match rates differ between the same-expansion comparison and the expansion-factor-4 comparison.

fits_no_version.finding: The synth-lead feature (text2midi L13 f3340) has a high-correlation counterpart in an earlier same-size dictionary (r=0.970/0.943) and an EF4 dictionary (r=0.980/0.962). Only 35.2% and 25.6% of final L13 features have a match at r≥0.8 on both splits.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features recur only partly across independently trained dictionaries of the same or different size; some interpretable features are highly stable while most are not.

record.problems: Each final dictionary is a single training run. The cross-dictionary recurrence result focuses on one feature, while the matching proportions use a thresholded nearest-feature match; neither establishes a general decomposition or splitting pattern.
record.rows_left_out: No further results were included: the remaining observational and intervention results concern musical metrics, instrument selection, descriptions, and steering rather than dictionary-size splitting or its predicted input partitions.

untested.parts: Whether a coarse feature is replaced by finer features covering its inputs and lying near its direction as dictionary size grows.
Splitting in large models or open SAE releases.
Nested, geometrically close feature families mirroring a concept hierarchy.
Parent latents failing to fire where child latents take over; persistence across size or sparsity.
Decomposition of larger-SAE latents into combinations of smaller-SAE latents, and novel latents in larger SAEs. The single-feature nearest-neighbour matches (r1–r4) do not measure this.
Whether the sparsity objective produces splitting, or whether alternative objectives such as Matryoshka change it.

record.verdict_notes: All four rows correctly carry versions ['none'] and the state cannot_determine. The study is not an original source. No verdict labels apply.

versions.untested_parts: Whether increasing dictionary size replaces a coarse feature with finer features that partition its inputs and lie near its direction.
Whether the splitting pattern holds in large models or open SAE releases.
Whether split features form nested, geometrically close families reflecting a concept hierarchy.
Whether parent latents fail to fire where child latents take over, and whether size or sparsity changes fail to fix this.
Whether larger-SAE latents decompose into combinations of smaller-SAE latents and larger SAEs add novel latents.
Whether the SAE objective produces splitting on correlated or hierarchical inputs, or whether Matryoshka SAEs change or reduce it.
